Guard Process use with #if os(macOS) || os(Linux). Otherwise throw GatewayProcessError.launchFailed(ENOTSUP), so iOS 17 builds still compile.

designDecisionsAndRationale: Use a new exchange helper instead of POSIXGatewayProcessRunner, because that runner closes stdin after writing and codex app-server exits on stdin EOF before it answers.

Write requests with gwp_write instead of FileHandle.write or transport.send. A dead reader would otherwise raise SIGPIPE or an uncatchable exception in the host, and with gwp_write EPIPE maps to the exited-without-answer path.
Treat stdout EOF, not terminationHandler, as the exit signal, so a response printed just before the child exits is still returned.
GatewayJSONLineExchangeError keeps the exchange independent of subscription-usage codes. The reader maps launchFailed, exitedWithoutAnswer and timedOut to -32041 messages that name the executable.
parseGatewayISO8601Date has package access and truncates fractions to 3 digits, because ISO8601DateFormatter rejects Claude's 6-digit fractions. This avoids widening the public API.
Claude model_scoped entries become weekly windows with the display name as scope. When model_scoped is absent, the legacy seven_day_opus/seven_day_sonnet keys are the fallback.
Codex rateLimitsByLimitId ordering puts the codex bucket first as plan-wide (scope nil) and sorts the other keys with scope limitName ?? limitId. When that map is absent, rateLimits is the fallback.
The validation order is fixed: protocol version, vendor, timeout, executable resolution, then exchange. No process is spawned before resolution.

Each plan owns a plan-unique generated-output root tmp/subscription-usage-build/<planId> (gitignored, excluded in .swiftlint.yml), listed in both writePaths and artifactRoots. Per-plan swift build/test/run use --scratch-path <root>, swiftlint uses --cache-path <root>/swiftlint-cache, and logs go to <root>/logs through plain redirection instead of tee, so echo exit=$? reports the real exit status. Only integration verification uses the default .build.
intentionalTradeoffs: A Codex initialize failure waits until the timeout (default 60 s) instead of failing early.

The vendor stdio protocols are undocumented (verified against claude 2.1.312 and codex-cli 0.166.0). The parsers tolerate missing and extra keys, and a shape change shows up as -32041 or as missing windows.
Wave-1 plans share one working tree, so implementers wait and retry on transient sibling compile failures instead of cross-editing.
The live claude-code and codex smokes depend on sandbox CLI and network access. If they are blocked, they are recorded as gaps, not passes.
Four separate scratch roots mean four cold SwiftPM builds (extra disk and time), in exchange for no .build contention between parallel implementers.
supportedEdgeCases: Claude rate_limits_available=false gives available=false and windows=[] with exit 0.
Claude error subtype gives -32041 with the vendor message.
Unrelated stdout lines (hook events, notifications, non-JSON) before the response are skipped.
Codex null primary or secondary windows and null buckets are skipped.
Codex JSON-RPC error gives -32041 with the vendor message.
A child exits without answering: -32041 with the stderr tail.
A child never answers: -32041 timeout, and the child is killed.
A missing executable gives -32041 executable unavailable.
An invalid protocolVersion or non-positive/non-finite timeoutSeconds gives -32602.
Unsupported vendors give -32040 before any executable resolution.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Vendor protocol versions other than those verified (claude 2.1.312, codex-cli 0.166.0) beyond tolerant parsing.
Platforms other than macOS and Linux at runtime (they throw ENOTSUP).
Live verification when the sandbox blocks the CLIs or the network (recorded as a gap).

Internal GatewayJSONLineExchangeError {launchFailed(String), exitedWithoutAnswer(stderrTail:), timedOut(seconds:)} and exchangeGatewayJSONLines(executable:arguments:environment:requests:timeoutSeconds:isResponse:) match the plan Contract exactly.
Stdin stays open until cleanup. Requests are written with gwp_write, with EINTR and partial-write handling. There are no FileHandle.write, transport.send or signal( calls.

Stdout EOF without a match gives exitedWithoutAnswer with a trimmed 2 KiB stderr tail. Timeout gives timedOut. Cleanup on every path is SIGTERM, then 2 s, then SIGKILL, then waitUntilExit and transport.close.
Process use is guarded by #if os(macOS) || os(Linux). Otherwise it throws GatewayProcessError.launchFailed(ENOTSUP).
